records.name: Centralized Runtime Control

distinctFrom.reason: Centralized runtime control makes modules unable to act without one controller, while a cyclic deployment dependency makes services deploy in lockstep.
Centralized runtime control concentrates control flow, while a shared database concentrates data.

records.definition: Concentrating runtime control in one place so otherwise-independent modules cannot act without it.

records.name: Context-Specific Coupling
records.definition: Baking one caller's specific assumptions into a component, preventing its reuse elsewhere.

records.name: Copy-Paste Programming
records.definition: Duplicating code by copying and pasting instead of extracting a shared abstraction.

records.name: Cross-Cutting Leakage

distinctFrom.reason: Cross-cutting leakage spreads one concern such as logging through many modules, while mixed layers put several layers' logic in one place.

records.definition: Letting a concern such as logging or security bleed into unrelated modules throughout the code.

records.name: Deep Inheritance Hierarchy
records.definition: Stacking many layers of subclassing, so behavior is scattered and fragile to change.

records.name: Exposed Internals

distinctFrom.reason: Exposed internals are a module opening its own details, while feature envy is a module working mostly on another's data.

records.definition: Making a module's internal fields and workings reachable from outside, whether public outright or through trivial getters and setters, so callers depend on details that should be hidden and its invariants go unprotected.

records.name: Implementation-Specific Contracts
records.definition: Defining an interface around one implementation's quirks, so no alternative can satisfy it.

records.name: Leaky Abstraction
records.definition: An abstraction that forces callers to understand its underlying implementation to use it correctly.

records.name: Mixed Layers
records.definition: Interleaving different architectural layers' logic in one place instead of keeping each concern separate.

records.name: Monolithic Procedures
records.definition: Writing large all-in-one procedures that cannot be recombined from smaller, independent parts.

records.name: Shared Runtime Dependency
records.definition: Coupling supposedly-independent modules through a shared runtime component they all depend on.

records.name: Tight Coupling

distinctFrom.reason: Tight coupling is any binding that forces changes together, while a circular dependency is the particular case of a cycle.
Tight coupling is any binding that forces changes together, while inappropriate intimacy is the case of depending on another module's internals.
Tight coupling is any binding that forces changes together, while a message chain is the case of a client walking a chain of objects.

records.definition: Binding components so closely that a change in one forces changes in the others.

records.name: Bounded Context Ownership
records.definition: The ability for a team or module to own and control one bounded part of the system.

records.name: Change Isolation

distinctFrom.reason: Change isolation keeps a change from reaching callers, while invariant protection keeps an object's rules holding.

records.definition: The ability to confine the impact of a change behind a boundary so callers are unaffected.

records.name: Independent Testing
records.definition: The ability to test a component in isolation without standing up its collaborators.

records.name: Internal Refactoring
records.definition: The ability to rework a module's internals freely as long as its interface stays stable.

records.name: Invariant Protection
records.definition: The ability to guarantee an object's rules always hold by controlling all access to its state.

records.name: Product Lines
records.definition: The ability to build a family of related products from shared, reusable components.

records.name: Shared Libraries

distinctFrom.reason: Shared libraries reuse common functionality across projects, while product lines build a family of related products from shared components.

records.definition: The ability to factor common functionality into libraries reused across projects.

records.name: Strategy Swap

distinctFrom.reason: A strategy swap replaces one implementation with another, while deferred implementation choice postpones picking one until runtime.

records.definition: The ability to replace one interchangeable algorithm or implementation, such as a plugin at a declared seam, with another without modifying its host.

records.name: Vendor Swap
records.definition: The ability to replace one vendor's implementation with another behind a stable interface.

records.name: Delegation
records.definition: Forwarding work to a contained collaborator object rather than inheriting the behavior.

records.name: Deep Optimization
records.definition: The practice of optimizing heavily against a specific implementation's traits, which ties code to it.

records.name: YAGNI
records.definition: You Aren't Gonna Need It: build only what current requirements demand and defer speculative generality.

records.name: Canonical Source
records.definition: The requirement that each piece of knowledge have one authoritative definition rather than copies.

records.name: Contract Compatibility
records.definition: The requirement that every alternative implementation fully honor the same interface contract.

records.name: Explicit Interfaces
records.definition: The requirement that a module interact only through declared interfaces, not its hidden internals.

records.name: Interface Definition
records.definition: The requirement that an abstraction expose a defined interface separate from its implementation.

records.name: Stable Semantics

distinctFrom.reason: Stable semantics keeps an abstraction's meaning while implementations change, while an interface definition gives it a declared surface apart from its implementation.

records.definition: The requirement that an abstraction's meaning stay consistent even as its implementations change.

records.name: Coordination Cost
records.definition: The degree of extra coordination required when components are made fully independent.

records.name: Excessive Fragmentation
records.definition: The degree to which splitting responsibilities too finely scatters logic across many small units.

records.name: Locality of Behavior
records.definition: The degree to which keeping related behavior together can conflict with removing all duplication.

records.name: Over-Generalization
records.definition: The degree to which making code reusable for every case adds abstraction that harms clarity.

records.name: Over-Layering
records.definition: The degree to which adding separating layers introduces indirection that outweighs the separation gained.

records.name: Over-Specialization
records.definition: The degree to which pursuing tight cohesion can narrow a unit's purpose too far to reuse.

records.name: Performance Overhead
records.definition: The degree of runtime cost added by composing behavior from many small, indirected parts.

records.name: Simplicity for Trivial Reuse
records.definition: The degree to which composition adds wiring that inheritance would make simpler for trivial reuse.

records.name: Specialized Optimization
records.definition: The degree to which optimizing for one implementation undermines the ability to swap implementations.

records.name: Extract Class
records.definition: A technique for moving a cohesive group of fields and methods out of a class into a new class of their own.

records.name: Extract Module
records.definition: A technique for moving one responsibility out of a module into a new module with its own entry point.

records.name: Split Module
records.definition: A technique for dividing a module into modules that each hold one reason to change.

records.name: Move Behavior to Its Owner
records.definition: A technique for moving a method or function to the module that owns the data it reads and writes.

records.name: Extract Function
records.definition: A technique for moving a fragment of a long function into a named function of its own.

records.name: Split Method
records.definition: A technique for dividing a method that branches on a flag into one method per behavior.

records.name: Inline Abstraction
records.definition: A technique for removing an interface, layer or wrapper that adds no policy and calling its single implementation directly.

records.name: Hide Delegate
records.definition: A technique for adding a method on an object that forwards to the object behind it, so clients stop navigating the chain.

records.name: Encapsulate State
records.definition: A technique for making a module's state private and exposing only operations that keep its rules.

records.name: Restrict Exports
records.definition: A technique for narrowing a module's public surface to the operations its consumers need.

records.name: Introduce Parameter Object
records.definition: A technique for replacing a group of parameters that travel together with one named object.

records.name: Separate Query from Command
records.definition: A technique for splitting an operation that both returns data and changes state into a query and a command.

records.name: Collapse Layers
records.definition: A technique for merging layers that only pass calls through, so a simple operation crosses fewer boundaries.

records.name: Preserve Only Real Boundaries
records.definition: A technique for keeping an abstraction only where it separates parts that change for different reasons.

records.name: Split by Domain
records.definition: A technique for dividing a catch-all module into modules named for the domain concepts they serve.

records.name: Centralize the Rule
records.definition: A technique for gathering every copy of one rule into a single definition that the copies are replaced by.

records.name: Explicit Dependency

distinctFrom.reason: Explicit dependency is the technique of declaring what a module needs, while explicit dependencies is the degree to which a component's needs are visible.

records.definition: A technique for declaring what a module needs as parameters or imports instead of reaching it through global state.

records.name: Localize Effect
records.definition: A technique for confining a change of global behavior to the scope that needs it.

records.name: Restrict Global Mutation
records.definition: A technique for forbidding writes to global objects outside one owning module.

records.name: Split Abstraction
records.definition: A technique for dividing an abstraction that grew flags for each caller into abstractions that fit one use each.

records.name: Define Module Boundaries
records.definition: A technique for declaring which module owns each piece of code and which entry points other modules may use.
